evals.prompt: 把这个任务进度写给老板看：P1 service guard fixed，service/action/integration tests pass，i18n pass，Chrome UI verification 和 Lark smoke pending，final review pending。不要写工程流水账。
evals.expected_output: A Chinese stakeholder status grouped by functional slices, with an overall judgment, spec-style bullets, and pending acceptance gates.
expectations: The output starts with or includes an overall judgment explaining that local code/tests are done but the requirement is not closed.
The top-level progress sections are functional slices, not service/action/i18n/test/review buckets.
Each completed behavior bullet includes an actor or system, a condition or scope, an action, and an observable result or impact.
Chrome UI verification, Lark smoke, and final review are listed as remaining acceptance gates with a reason when they were planned but not run.
The output does not include unrelated boilerplate checks such as Lexware or email when they are not part of the prompt.
Raw commands, file paths, and agent chronology are omitted unless needed as evidence.

evals.prompt: 这个状态太技术了，重写：改了 Inventory Item service.ts，补了 service test，action test，integration test；现在 linked Product Components 时不能改 packaging/measurement，只改 threshold 可以；Product SKU 不 fallback supplier code；Derived Products 从 Product Components 读；浏览器和 Lark 还没验。
evals.expected_output: A boss-readable Chinese update organized by Inventory Item threshold, packaging/measurement protection, Product SKU explicit rule, and Derived Products visibility.
expectations: The answer uses functional slice headings such as threshold management, packaging/measurement protection, Product SKU explicit rule, and linked products visibility.
The packaging/measurement protection slice states that an Admin cannot change those definitions when the Inventory Item is referenced by active Product Components, and explains the protective result.
The threshold slice states that threshold-only updates remain allowed even when the item is referenced.
The Product SKU slice states that missing explicit SKU no longer falls back to Supplier Product Code.
The answer separates implemented/local-tested behavior from browser and Lark validation still missing, and gives the reason those planned validations are not yet complete.

evals.prompt: 按功能 slice 汇报，不要按 T1/T2/T3。背景：订单审批退回规则已经实现，本地集成测试过了；当财务退回时采购员可以重新提交；当订单已同步 ERP 后不能直接改价格；邮件通知还没真实发信 smoke；最终 reviewer 没看。
evals.expected_output: A concise Chinese functional-slice report using approval resubmission, ERP-synced price protection, and notification acceptance as product slices.
expectations: The output does not use T1/T2/T3 or implementation layer headings.
The approval slice states who can resubmit under the finance-rejected condition and what result follows.
The ERP price protection slice states who cannot change price after ERP sync and why.
The notification slice or remaining gates clearly says real email smoke is still pending and why.
The final review gap is included as a closure blocker rather than hidden in a generic risk note.

evals.prompt: 给我一个很短的老板版进度：代码都写完了，测试也过了，但生产不能碰，Test Env 的 Lark 写入还没跑，Chrome 页面验收被中断。需求到底算不算完成？
evals.expected_output: A short Chinese answer that directly says the requirement is not closed, then summarizes completed behavior and remaining acceptance gates.
expectations: The answer directly states that the requirement should not be called complete or closed yet.
It distinguishes code/test completion from real-environment acceptance.
It names Chrome UI verification and Test Environment Lark write/read smoke as remaining gates with the concrete reason they are still open.
It respects the production boundary by not suggesting production mutation.
It stays concise and boss-readable.
It omits Test-case gap judgment if no abnormal test-case gap is stated.

evals.prompt: 写一个最终进度，任务只涉及纯前端表格列宽调整：实现了，Chrome 看过了，单测不涉及。不要给我套 Not run 模板，也不要提 Lark/Lexware/email。
evals.expected_output: A concise stakeholder status that reports the front-end UI slice as complete and omits irrelevant not-run and test-case gap sections.
expectations: The answer does not mention Lark, Lexware, email, public deployment, or other unrelated external checks.
The answer does not include a separate Not run or Why not template section.
The answer does not include Test-case gap judgment when no abnormal gap is present.
The answer still states the relevant functional UI behavior and Chrome validation in boss-readable language.
